topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, outlining the lecture's historical perspective, structure, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, oncogene discovery, and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of viral transmission in cancer revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental methods for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and classifications of oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer mutations are categorised by their functional effects and illustrate these concepts through key cell-cycle regulators such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and forms of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish between sequence and chromosomal instability while detailing the specific DNA repair and mitotic errors that cause them.

topics.label: Stepwise tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic alterations drive cancer development and how inherited mutations accelerate this multi-step process.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, concluding the session with reading suggestions and an overview of the next lecture.
